title: Flee 3: Flexible agent-based simulation for forced migration

key_points.claim: Flee 3 is an ABM for forced migration that supports group-specific forecasts (children, ethnicity, religion) rather than only headline arrival numbers.
key_points.evidence_quote: lack the flexibility to explore migration patterns for specific groups, such as children or persons of a specific ethnicity or religion

key_points.claim: Agent rules for movement and creation are adaptable. The model includes food security, ethnicity, religion, gender and age. This enables models of internal displacement and non-conflict migration.
key_points.evidence_quote: introduces adaptable rules for agent movement and creation, along with a more refined model that flexibly supports factors like food security, ethnicity, religion, gender and/or age

key_points.claim: Validation on ten historical conflicts in Asia and Africa against UNHCR data gave an error below 0.6, i.e. over 70% of refugee arrivals forecast correctly. It beat the predecessor in all but one case.
key_points.evidence_quote: validation error (averaged relative difference) of less than 0.6 in all cases, i.e. correctly forecasting over 70% of refugee arrivals

key_points.claim: Scalability: the parallel code simulates the Ukraine 2022 conflict in under an hour with 80% parallel efficiency on 512 cores.
key_points.evidence_quote: simulate migration from a large scale conflict (Ukraine 2022) in less than an hour and with 80% parallel efficiency using 512 cores per run

key_points.claim: Two practitioner use cases (a research project and an NGO). The code is open source.
key_points.evidence_quote: we present two use cases: one involving an international migration research project and one involving an international NGO

reliability_notes: Abstract only. The fetched page gave metadata and abstract, and I saw no full text. Peer-reviewed software paper. It is a domain-specific ABM (migration), not a general artificial-society paper.
